newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rioting Brazil inmates free seven guards.
newsitem.headline: Rioting Brazil inmates free seven guards.

text.p: Seven guards were freed Thursday but three others remain captives of knife-wielding inmates who took over a prison in southern Brazil two days ago, police said.
"They released seven hostages today. Three remain," police Sgt. Roberto Camargo told Reuters.

The freed hostages were not physically hurt but were "psychologically distressed" as a result of being held hostage since Tuesday by prisoners at a prison in Florianopolis, capital of Santa Catarina state, he said.
The atmosphere around the siege site was "calm, tranquil" late Thursday following the transfer over two days of some 180 inmates as part of a deal to end the uprising, Camargo said.
Some 295 inmates armed with stilletos, hammers and skewers seized the prison and took 10 guards hostage on Tuesday morning, complaining of torture, protesting overcrowding and demanding transfers.

Authorities began transferring inmates on Tuesday as vacancies came open at other facilities under an agreement with inmates to end the uprising bloodlessly. The inmates had threatened to execute the guards if police tried to attack to rescue the hostages.
Officials are continuing to search for space at other prisons for the remaining roughly 100 prisoners and have begun investigating the incident to begin charging those responsible, Camargo said.
The uprising was one of three jail rebellions on Tuesday and one of five in two days at Brazil's notoriously overcrowded prisons.
Camargo said authorities are investigating the incident at Florianopolis to begin charging those responsible for the uprising.
